conventions.convention: The inverse determinant line is (det_C ker D+) dual tensor det_C coker D+, including det 0 = C. This is Dai–Freed's Det convention; their inverse-line transport must be dualized before comparison.
A loop uses a path A0 to A1 and a forward endpoint gauge arrow u:A0→A1; holonomy is the scalar of u_* inverse composed with parallel transport.
Spectral-cut gluing, zeta continuation, heat finite parts, metric compatibility and gauge naturality are supplied admissible analytic data, rather than consequences of Fredholmness alone.

Boundary orientation is outward-normal-first. Mapping-torus orientation is or(M) followed by dt. The adopted closed bulk response equals bulk-line holonomy, and cancellation requires the product of boundary and bulk holonomies to equal one.
The central gauge clutch −1 combined with an antiperiodic spin clutch gives periodic total spinors. The same gauge clutch with periodic spin clutch gives antiperiodic total spinors.

Full AC is assumed for the product-kernel calculation and concrete round benchmark. The round positive-spin twist has index one, Chern number −1 and positive trace-form charge one. The determinant-line model is explicitly not identified with a fermionic Pfaffian-line model.

Vanishing of the adopted degree-six characteristic polynomial does not establish vanishing of the local BRST anomaly without a descent premise; even-copy triviality is asserted only for the tested loop.

load_bearing.statement: The closed-loop automorphism is u_* inverse composed with PT on the initial inverse determinant-line fiber. Its scalar is the holonomy Hol_gamma(L) ∈ U(1). The regularization and local-counterterm convention are fixed before comparison with the infinitesimal local anomaly.

The boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along gamma exactly when Hol_gamma(L_boundary) Hol_gamma(L_bulk) = 1. Identification of the closed mapping-torus response with bulk-line holonomy is adopted bulk/line data.

For the stipulated index-one SU(2) inverse-determinant-line background and central order-two loop, with full AC and the specified periodic total-spinor product realization, N≥1 copies have boundary holonomy (−1)^N and adopted mod-two-index bulk phase (−1)^N, hence combined holonomy +1. The adopted polynomial I6 vanishes. The combined unit weight on the ordinary finite test groupoid BC2 has normalized sum 1/2. These conclusions concern only the stated test.

seams_checked.note: The cited definition supplies only the infinitesimal local background-anomaly quotient. The assigned items explicitly exclude deriving global holonomy or local BRST cancellation from it.
The finite normalization check respects the prerequisite's invariant scalar-weight requirement and ordinary groupoid normalization. It makes no higher-group gluing or continuum-gauging claim.

The round index-one and periodic-product lemmas support the stated kernel dimensions, central action and clutch distinction. Full AC, reduction-compatible connection, charge/Chern sign and draft proof status are retained.
The associated quotient relation [pg,v]=[p,R(g)v], local formula dψ+dR(A)ψ and Countable Choice hypothesis agree with the associated-covariant-derivative supplier.
The example uses the actual round positive-spin twist, index one, Chern number −1 and periodic real-kernel parity one, with full AC and the same central test.

The RG theorem preserves the selected inverse-line convention and explicitly assumes connection- and gauge-compatible line comparison. The open problem treats categorical extension as an unresolved compatibility problem rather than an established consequence.
